# 3-Day Cold-Comfort Plan for Staying Functional

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/thermometer-half.svg
You likely have a mild viral upper-respiratory illness, with seasonal allergies possibly adding to the runny nose. The goal is to reduce throat pain, control drainage, and keep you hydrated enough to work.

# Best OTC Plan Under $30

## What to buy and use
- **Acetaminophen or ibuprofen** for fever, throat pain, and general aches
- **Saline nasal spray** or rinse for congestion and post-nasal drip
- **Honey** or lozenges for sore throat relief
- **Cetirizine or loratadine** if allergy symptoms are clearly contributing
- **Fluids with electrolytes** if you’re not eating/drinking much

## Simple OTC shopping list
- **Acetaminophen**: 500–1000 mg every 6–8 hours as needed; do not exceed the label maximum
- **Ibuprofen**: 200–400 mg every 6–8 hours with food as needed; avoid if you have stomach ulcers, kidney disease, or are dehydrated
- **Saline spray/rinse**: use several times daily, especially before work and before bed
- **Honey/lozenges**: use as needed for throat comfort
- **Cetirizine 10 mg or loratadine 10 mg once daily**: helpful if sneezing/itchy eyes are part of the picture; cetirizine can make some people sleepy

## Best-value combo
- If you want to stay functional at work, a practical low-cost mix is:
  - pain/fever reducer
  - saline nasal spray
  - honey/lozenges
  - one non-drowsy antihistamine only if allergy symptoms are prominent

## Safety notes
- Don’t combine multiple products that all contain acetaminophen.
- If you choose ibuprofen, take it with food and plenty of water.
- Rest, fluids, and symptom control matter more than “cold/flu” multi-symptom products, which often cost more and can cause drowsiness.

# When to Seek Medical Care

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/phone.svg
Most mild viral illnesses improve within a few days. Get medical advice sooner if symptoms start pointing away from a routine cold or if you’re getting worse instead of better.

## Symptoms that should prompt care
- Fever **≥ 103°F / 39.4°C**, or any fever lasting more than about **3 days**
- Trouble breathing, wheezing, chest pain, or shortness of breath
- Severe throat pain with trouble swallowing saliva, drooling, or muffled voice
- One-sided throat swelling, neck swelling, or severe ear pain
- Signs of dehydration: very dark urine, dizziness, dry mouth, inability to keep fluids down
- Symptoms that improve then suddenly worsen again
- A sore throat with **no cough** plus fever and swollen tender neck nodes, which can suggest strep
- Symptoms lasting **more than 10 days** without improvement
- New rash, confusion, or marked weakness
- If you’ve had close exposure to flu/COVID and symptoms fit, testing can help guide work decisions

## Good reasons to test or call a clinician
- You need to know whether this is COVID, flu, or strep for work or household contacts
- Fever persists or throat pain becomes severe
- You have a history of frequent strep, sinus infections, or asthma symptoms with colds

# 3-Day Rest-and-Hydration Schedule

## Day 1: Reduce symptoms and protect work capacity
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- **Morning:** Warm drink, saline spray, then take your chosen fever/pain medicine if needed
- **Work hours:** Sip water
